description: Booking Holdings Inc., together with its subsidiaries, provides online and traditional travel and restaurant reservations and related services in the United States, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom
description_full: Booking Holdings Inc., together with its subsidiaries, provides online and traditional travel and restaurant reservations and related services in the United States, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, and internationally. The company operates Booking.com, which offers online accommodation reservations; and Priceline, which provides discount travel reservations services, as well as online accommodation, flight, rental car reservation services, vacation packages, cruises, activity, and affiliate programs. It also operates Agoda that offers online accommodation reservation, flight, ground transportation, and attractions. In addition, the company operates KAYAK, an online meta-search service that allows consumers to search and compare travel itineraries and prices; and OpenTable for booking online restaurant reservations, as well as reservation management services to restaurants. Further, it offers travel-related insurance products, payment facilitation, and restaurant management services to consumers, travel service providers, and restaurants; and advertising services. The company was formerly known as The Priceline Group Inc. and changed its name to Booking Holdings Inc. in February 2018. Booking Holdings Inc. was founded in 1997 and is headquartered in Norwalk, Connecticut.

financial_summary: Booking Holdings Inc. Common St is a large-cap consumer cyclical business with a $119.5B market cap on $26.9B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +16% over the past three years and +11% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 37% against a 10% cost of capital — a 27-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 87% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $9.1B in free cash flow — roughly 34 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.74× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -13.7% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.2× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 5.5×.

Management returns a meaningful 6.4% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 4.0× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 33% operating margin runs 25pp above the Consumer Cyclical median (8%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 3.97x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
It accounts for 0.5% of sector revenue and 2.0% of sector operating profit.
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 377 companies in the universe; the top four hold 26% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted lower, down 19% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 27% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 39% and a beta of 1.12, it moves roughly with the market.
Liquidity is deep, with about $1.1B traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 45% in the 2020 crash, 40% in the 2022 bear market and 66% in 2008.
val: The stock trades only 12% below its DCF fair value of $183, a thin margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 18%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $143 to $238 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Consumer Cyclical peers: P/FCF 13.1 vs 16.5 (sector median).
The EBIT multiple is close to its own 10-year median (-3%).
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 7.6% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 6.7% (vs the 8% bar).
The 35 covering analysts target $227 on average, 41% above the price.
prof: ROIC of 37% clears the cost of capital of 9.9% by 27pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 2.10).
It runs a 87% gross margin and converts 34% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality is mixed: cash conversion of 1.74x, but high accruals (-13.7% of assets).
Operating margin is running 6pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 2.3% of revenue on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 0.2x net debt to EBITDA ($17.2B of cash against $18.7B of debt), with interest covered 5.5x.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 16.3% over 3 years, 31.7% over 5 years and 11.3% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 25%).
At current returns, reinvesting 6% of profits supports about 2.2% a year of fundamental growth, too little to drive meaningful growth.
Capex runs only 0.5x depreciation (1.2% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 63, clearing the bar for a healthy growth business.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 3.5% on average.
Analysts expect 18.1% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.2%), and institutions hold 99%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (26 sales, net $27.7M sold).
It returns 6.4% a year to shareholders (5.4% in buybacks and 1.0% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 6.2% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 25,850 employees, each generates about $1.0M of revenue, 2.7x the Consumer Cyclical median, and productivity has risen 15.5% a year.
That works out to $352K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $9.2M (9x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (3/10, lower is better).
